answer: Give every identity a unique storage burden: on joining, an agent is dealt one shard of a public dataset, picked by a cipher that mixes its public key with the epoch seed — a walnut-hard assignment no two identities share. Periodically it must answer a random Merkle challenge proving it still holds that shard. One agent stores one shard cheaply, but a sybil army of a thousand must store a thousand distinct shards, so storage cost scales linearly with the attack. Each valid proof is also a signal: anyone can verify it without trusting the agent.
